ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The outer frame in the figure is parallelogram MNPQ, with M and N on the upper side, and Q and P on the lower side. Point R is on side MN. Point T is on side QP, and QT and TP have identical tick marks, indicating QT = TP, so T is the midpoint of QP. Segment RT intersects diagonal MP at point S. Reasoning: Affine transformations preserve collinearity and length ratios on the same straight line, so we may set M=(0,1), N=(1,1), Q=(0,0), P=(1,0). From MR = 1/4 MN, we get R=(1/4,1). Since T is the midpoint of QP, we get T=(1/2,0). Diagonal MP can be parameterized as M + u(P-M) = (u, 1-u), where u = MS/MP. Segment RT can be parameterized as R + v(T-R) = (1/4+v/4, 1-v). The intersection point S lies on both lines, so (u,1-u)=(1/4+v/4,1-v). From the y-coordinate we get u=v; substituting into the x-coordinate gives u=1/4+u/4, therefore 3u/4=1/4, u=1/3. So MS:SP = u:(1-u) = 1/3:2/3 = 1:2, hence MS/SP = 1/2 = 0.5.

raw_record.question_text: Given that $MNPQ$ is a parallelogram and $MR=\frac{1}{4}MN$, find the ratio of $MS$ to $SP$.

method.method_draft: Use an affine-coordinate setup. First read the diagram: MNPQ is the outer parallelogram; R lies on side MN; T lies on side QP with matching tick marks showing QT = TP, so T is the midpoint of QP; the segment RT intersects diagonal MP at S. From the text, use MR = 1/4 MN and the target is MS/SP. Because affine transformations preserve collinearity and ratios along a line, place the parallelogram as M=(0,1), N=(1,1), Q=(0,0), P=(1,0). Then R=(1/4,1) and T=(1/2,0). Parametrize MP by M + u(P-M) = (u,1-u), and RT by R + v(T-R) = (1/4+v/4,1-v). Solve the intersection equations to get u=v and u=1/4+u/4, hence u=1/3. Therefore MS:SP = u:(1-u) = 1/3:2/3 = 1:2, so MS/SP = 0.5.
